entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pausanias of Orestis was a member of Philip II of Macedon's personal bodyguard (somatophylakes) and assassinated him in 336 BC. This event marked a pivotal moment in Macedonian history, as it led to the ascension of Alexander the Great to the throne. Pausanias' actions also had significant repercussions for the ancient Greek world, particularly for the city-states of Greece and the Hellenistic kingdoms that would soon follow.

Pausanias' assassination was a culmination of the tensions between Philip II and his own bodyguards, who had grown increasingly dissatisfied with his rule. The event also marked the beginning of a period of turmoil and power struggles in Macedon, as various factions vied for control.

The legacy of Pausanias' actions can still be seen in the ancient Greek world, where his assassination served as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of loyalty to one's ruler. In the centuries that followed, Pausanias' name became synonymous with treachery and betrayal, a reminder of the devastating consequences of his actions.

The assassination of Philip II also had far-reaching consequences for the ancient world, as it set in motion a chain of events that would shape the course of history. The rise of Alexander the Great, in particular, had a profound impact on the ancient world, as he went on to conquer a vast portion of the known world and establish one of the largest empires in history.

Pausanias of Orestis' story serves as a reminder of the complex and often fraught nature of power struggles in ancient history, where loyalty, ambition, and betrayal were all intertwined. His actions, though motivated by a desire for power and recognition, had far-reaching consequences that would be felt for centuries to come.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pausanias' assassination of Philip II marked a pivotal moment in Macedonian history and had significant repercussions for the ancient Greek world. The event set in motion a chain of events that would shape the course of history and leave a lasting impact on the ancient Greek world.
